fact: Mmegi reports that the Information and Data Protection Commission issued a determination and enforcement order finding the DPSM E-Payslip portal not fully compliant with the Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024, and DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.
Mmegi reports in July 2026 that Botswana continues to implement the Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024, under which the Commission monitors compliance and issues enforcement orders.
The Information and Data Protection Commission is acting: it reviewed the E-Payslip portal, issued a determination and enforcement order, and guided DPSM through compliance in July 2026.
The Commission's enforcement order against DPSM and the portal's suspension in July 2026 are a first reported enforcement against a public body in the report.

In a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the Information and Data Protection Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM for contraventions of the Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024, ordering the ePayslip portal suspended and a DPIA and revised privacy notice submitted within one month, with an administrative fine possible for non-compliance.
The Commission enforced Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024 against DPSM in July 2026, citing its provisions including Section 52 on data protection by design and by default.
The Information and Data Protection Commission issued a public notice with a Determination and Enforcement Notice on 17 July 2026, showing it acting.

The Commission's enforcement notice of 17 July 2026 against DPSM is described as its first published enforcement action against a government body (sweep note, not part of the source, so only the notice itself is relied on).
Mmegi reports that Kepaletswe Somolekae is the newly appointed Information and Data Protection Commissioner, as at 11 February 2026.
Mmegi states the Data Protection Act came into force in January 'last year' (2025) after years of a grace period and applies to all organisations processing personal data, including public entities.
A new Information and Data Protection Commissioner was appointed by February 2026 and vowed firmer enforcement against non-bank financial institutions.
The Minister for State President told Parliament on 29 July 2025 that the Data Protection Act's implementation started on 14 January 2025.

The Minister stated the Information and Data Protection Commission was established in 2022 and its commissioner had employed three contract officers, while the Deputy Commissioner and two director posts were unfilled and the structure awaited approval.
TechHive Advisory states Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024, published 29 October 2024, took effect on 14 January 2025 and repeals the Data Protection Act No. 32 of 2018, which never came into force.

fact: Statutory Instrument No. 86 of 2021, made 24 September 2021 by the Minister for Presidential Affairs, Governance and Public Administration, brought the Data Protection Act (Act No. 32 of 2018) into operation on the date of the Order's publication, 15 October 2021.

Statutory Instrument No. 4 of 2025, made by the Minister for State President on 13 January 2025, provides that the Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 18 of 2024) comes into operation on 14 January 2025.
